source_name: Slovak Fintech Association – Eventy / Novinky
why_relevant: Association hub listing SK fintech events and news; member and event-partner lists are a standing pointer to vendors selling compliance, payments and identity tooling into SK banks, and to bank-fintech partnership announcements.

source_name: Finweek Bratislava – conference programme & partners
why_relevant: SK fintech/banking conference; programme and partner/sponsor pages reveal which vendors are actively selling to SK banks and which bank executives own which compliance programmes — a classic indirect procurement-signal source.

source_name: IBV NBS – FinNext conference
why_relevant: Conference run by the NBS-affiliated Institute of Banking Education, mixing NBS regulators, financial-institution leaders and fintech vendors. Speaker/partner rosters link regulatory agenda items to the vendors positioning against them — useful bridge between A3 regulation topics and vendor ecosystem.

source_name: FinStat – company financials & Obchodný register mirror (vendor and bank entities)
why_relevant: Reveals SK vendor entities indirectly: revenue trajectories, name history (e.g. Asseco Central Europe, historically Asseco Slovakia), and corporate links. Useful to size vendors and detect entity changes, and to cross-check that a claimed SK vendor actually operates locally. Does not itself name bank contracts.

source_name: Protimonopolný úrad SR – decisions (merger/competition case files)
why_relevant: Antitrust decision PDFs on IT-sector and financial-sector cases describe supplier market structure, bidding behaviour and customer relationships in detail that vendors never publish. A rare route into private-sector buying behaviour.

source_name: European Commission – merger case files involving SK banks (e.g. M.10378 VUB / Slovenska sporitelna / Tatra banka)
why_relevant: EU merger filings for SK bank joint ventures describe shared infrastructure/service arrangements between the three systemic private banks — evidence of joint procurement and shared-vendor arrangements that no public portal covers.

source_name: 365.bank group structure page (skupina 365.bank)
why_relevant: Bank-published group structure identifies the legal entities inside the 365.bank / Poštová banka group — the buying units a vendor case study would name, and the entities to match against supplier announcements.

source_name: APIS – Referencie
why_relevant: SK vendor publishing a customer reference list surfaced by the local-language 'referencie' sweep; candidate for the mid-tier supplier bench serving financial institutions. Bank-specific content not yet confirmed — collect and verify.

source_name: ÚVO – Vyhľadávanie zákaziek (Public Procurement Office tender search)
why_relevant: Central national search over all Slovak public procurement notices. Filtering by contracting authority (NBS, MF SR, Štátna pokladnica, state banks) and by CPV codes for software/consulting surfaces tender texts that name the regulation being implemented (DORA, PSD2/PSD3, AML, IFRS/FINREP-COREP reporting) and its compliance deadline, typically months before public announcement.

source_name: Vestník verejného obstarávania (ÚVO Public Procurement Bulletin)
why_relevant: The official daily bulletin of procurement notices submitted via the eForms system. It is the authoritative, dated publication stream — ideal as a daily-diff feed for new notices from financial-sector public bodies; the publication date anchors a timeline of upcoming regulatory implementations.

source_name: ÚVO profil verejného obstarávateľa – Národná banka Slovenska (profile #8643)
why_relevant: The single highest-value profile in this cell: all NBS procurement documents in one place. NBS is both central bank and integrated financial supervisor, so its IT/consulting tenders directly reveal which supervisory, reporting, resolution or payment-oversight obligations it is building for and by when.

source_name: NBS – Verejné obstarávanie / Profil verejného obstarávateľa
why_relevant: NBS's own procurement hub, confirming it runs above-threshold tenders through IS JOSEPHINE and linking to sub-sections for selected tenders, contracts/orders/invoices, and preparatory market consultations. Gives the routing map for where NBS demand signals appear.

source_name: NBS – Prípravné trhové konzultácie (preparatory market consultations)
why_relevant: Earliest-possible signal in the procurement lifecycle. A PTK is published before a tender exists and describes the intended system and the driving obligation — this is where a future supervisory-reporting or payments-oversight requirement first becomes visible in writing.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (Slovakia filter)
why_relevant: All above-threshold Slovak notices are mirrored to TED in structured eForms XML, with English summaries. Better machine-readability and cross-border comparability than ÚVO — lets the same regulatory-driven tender be compared against peer central banks/supervisors in CZ, PL, HU.

source_name: TED Search API / bulk XML packages
why_relevant: The programmable ingestion path for the whole cell. Documented, unauthenticated, supports expert queries, pagination up to 15k docs and an unlimited paging token, plus daily/monthly bulk XML packages — the cheapest way to build a persistent longitudinal index of SK financial-sector tenders.

source_name: IS EVO / Elektronická platforma verejného obstarávania (EPVO) – portál zákaziek
why_relevant: The state-operated e-procurement platform (transferred to the Government Office in March 2022) through which many public bodies actually run procedures. Its public order search exposes tender documentation and Q&A ('vysvetlenia') that often contain the most explicit statements of regulatory scope and deadline.

source_name: JOSEPHINE (PROEBIZ) – public tenders list, used by NBS
why_relevant: NBS's own procurement page states that its above-threshold tenders are conducted via IS JOSEPHINE. The platform's public tender list therefore carries NBS (and other financial bodies') live tender records and attached documentation, sometimes visible earlier or in fuller form than the ÚVO profile.

source_name: EKS – Elektronický kontraktačný systém / elektronické trhovisko
why_relevant: Central electronic marketplace for below-threshold contracts and dynamic purchasing systems. Small advisory, legal-analysis and reporting-tool purchases by ministries and supervisors land here rather than on TED — a low-value but high-frequency early indicator of regulatory workstreams.

source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ) – Central Register of Contracts
why_relevant: Statutory register where every contract of ministries, central state bodies and public-law institutions must be published to take effect (Act 546/2010). Signed contract texts are far more explicit than notices: scope of work, milestone dates, named regulations, and the vendor actually delivering the supervisory/reporting system.

source_name: UVOstat – aggregated ÚVO + CRZ analytics and API
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator joining procurement notices, the contract register and buyer-supplier relationships into one queryable dataset with an API. Dramatically reduces the cost of longitudinal analysis (who supplies NBS/MF SR regulatory IT, at what cadence).

source_name: Verejné súťaže portal (EPVO + EKS + ÚVO aggregation)
why_relevant: Aggregates tenders from EPVO, EKS, ZNH and ÚVO into one searchable feed, useful as a cross-check that no channel was missed. Individual tender pages (e.g. ÚVO IT staffing and IS upgrade contracts) are indexed and readable.

source_name: Tender.sk – commercial tender intelligence platform (SK + abroad)
why_relevant: Commercial platform with CPV/region/buyer/keyword search and an integration API. Its taxonomy and saved-search alerting can be used to prototype the CPV filter set before building in-house ingestion from ÚVO/TED.

source_name: MetaIS – Centrálny metainformačný systém verejnej správy (register of public-administration IT systems and projects)
why_relevant: Upstream of procurement: public bodies must register planned IT assets, project intents (projektový zámer) and change requests here before tendering, under Vyhláška 401/2023 Z.z. on IT project management. A registered ISVS or projektový zámer for a supervisory/reporting system is the earliest structured evidence that an obligation is being operationalised, with its planned timeline.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR – Centrálny register zmlúv resort view
why_relevant: MF SR is the transposing ministry for EU financial-services directives. Its contracts for legal analyses, transposition studies and impact assessments name the directive being transposed and the transposition deadline — often before any public consultation opens.

source_name: Open Data MF SR (opendata.mfsr.sk)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance open-data portal; useful for machine-readable budget/contract/organisation datasets that let procurement records be joined to budget lines, indicating the scale and timing of a regulatory implementation programme.

source_name: EXIMBANKA SR – Profil verejného obstarávateľa
why_relevant: State export-import bank; a contracting authority whose IT and compliance tenders (AML/CFT screening, sanctions, reporting) reveal which prudential and financial-crime obligations state-linked lenders are implementing and on what schedule.

source_name: Slovenská konsolidačná, a.s. – Obstarávanie
why_relevant: State-owned NPL/receivables consolidation company. Its procurement reveals state handling of distressed financial assets and any data/reporting systems it must build — an indirect but distinctive read on receivables and recovery regulation.

source_name: Štátna pokladnica – CRZ contract listing
why_relevant: The State Treasury operates core payment and settlement infrastructure for the public sector. Its contracts and tenders track payment-scheme migrations (SEPA/ISO 20022, instant payments) and their mandated cut-over dates — a direct read on payments-regulation timing.

source_name: ÚVO – Vestník a Registre (registers hub)
why_relevant: Hub for all registers ÚVO maintains under Act 343/2015 (bulletin, profiles, register of final beneficial owners / partners of the public sector). Beyond tender discovery, this supports vendor due-diligence and mapping who actually supplies regulatory systems to the Slovak financial state.
